exposure: Body mass index (BMI) based on the Working Group on Obesity in China (WGOC) definitions
outcome: Preterm premature rupture of the membranes (PPROM)
cohort: Singleton births from first fresh IVF cycle between January 2014 and December 2016 at the Reproductive Center affiliated to Shandong University (N = 3,962)
finding: Pregravid overweight and obesity independently predicted a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes after adjusting for maternal age, parity, PCOS, and type of COH in IVF pregnancies.
mod_finding: For obese women, a 10%-15% reduction in prepregnancy BMI was associated with significantly decreased risks of GH, CS and fetal macrosomia, while for overweight women, a 5% reduction in BMI could significantly reduce the risks of GDM, CS and fetal macrosomia.
birth_weight: Fetal macrosomia, large for gestational age (LGA) >90th percentile, small for gestational age (SGA) >90th percentile
